where $\tilde{c}_{d,k} > 0$ is a universal constant depending only on $d$ and $k$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Clenshaw–Curtis weights defined in the paper, and the cited Novak–Ritter estimate, concern integration against Lebesgue measure. The theorem instead claims the bound for integration against a general factorized ν with L^p densities, with a constant independent of ν. No ν-weighted rule is constructed and no weighted error bound is proved. The affine rescaling by ((b-a)/2)^d is the Lebesgue rescaling. Applied to a probability measure ν, it makes the weights sum to ((b-a)/2)^d (2^{-d} on [0,1]^d) rather than 1, so even constants are integrated incorrectly.

The scaling and the constant's dependence on ν must be fixed accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The quadrature-error bound is unsupported for non-uniform (or non-Lebesgue-normalized) ν. This includes the general factorized ν allowed by Assumption main_assumptions and used in the main theorem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The target class $\mathcal{T} \subset \mathcal{M}_1^+([0,1]^d)$ consists of absolutely continuous measures with densities $f_\mu \in C^k([0,1]^d)$.
and that $\|u^\mu\|_{C^1}$ can be bounded by a constant $c_{d,\kappa,\mathcal{K}}$ by~\cite[Theorem 4.12]{marzouk2025} depending only on $d,\kappa,\mathcal{K}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The assumption bounds the densities only in sup norm (between κ and 𝒦), not in C^k norm. Take f_μ = 1 + ½ sin(2πN x_1)g(x), with N→∞. Then κ and 𝒦 stay fixed, but derivatives of the Knothe–Rosenblatt map grow with N: T'' involves f_μ', and for d≥2 the off-diagonal ∂_{x_1}T_2 involves ∂_{y_1}f_μ. Hence sup_μ‖u^μ⊘η_d‖_{C^k}, and even ‖u^μ‖_{C^1}, cannot be bounded by a constant depending only on d,k,κ,𝒦. The constants in the theorem, the depth requirement through log₂log₂ c, and hence the model-error threshold all depend on μ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to Assumption main_assumptions a uniform bound sup_{μ∈𝒯}‖f_μ‖_{C^k} ≤ 𝒦 (and similarly for ν). Make all constants depend on it, as in the cited regularity results.
issues.overall_effect: Uniformity over 𝒯 of the model-error bound fails. The main theorem's PAC claim 'for all μ∈𝒯' with μ-independent thresholds is unsupported.
issues.title: Uniform-in-μ C^k (and C^1) bounds on target vector fields without any uniform bound on density derivatives
issues.why_classification: A standard extra hypothesis restores the argument but materially narrows the target class from all C^k densities with two-sided bounds to a C^k ball.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed inequality |log|det A| − log|det B|| ≤ Σ_k C(d,k)2^k‖A−B‖^k is false in general. For A=εI and B=2εI the left side is d log 2, while the right side is (1+2ε)^d − 1 → 0. A determinant perturbation bound controls |det A − det B| with factors depending on the singular values of A. Passing to logarithms requires a lower bound on |det|, which is never supplied. The same step is used in the sub-Gaussian lemma and in the bounded-difference estimate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We bound the first integral by our Lipschitz sensitivity bounds

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lip_constants gives Lipschitz dependence on θ at a fixed point (x,t). The two Jacobians here are evaluated at different points [Φ_t^θ]^{-1}(x) and [Φ_t^{θ'}]^{-1}(x). Bounding their difference also requires a spatial Lipschitz constant of D_xṽ^{θ'} multiplied by the trajectory difference. The paper provides no such bound: only C^1 control (Corollary c1_bound) is available, and ReQU nets are merely C^{1,1}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a new lemma bounding the spatial Lipschitz constant of D_x v^θ for ReQU nets with parameters in [-1,1], of double-exponential form in L. Add the resulting term to the Gronwall argument and recheck that L̄ remains ≤ c·exp((c_dW)^{2^{2L+3}}).
issues.overall_effect: The sub-Gaussian constant L̄, and hence the expected generalization bound and the main PAC theorem, rest on an unproved estimate.

issues.failure_explanation: ε^gen is the supremum of the absolute value of Z_θ, so the equality with E[sup_θ Z_θ] is false. Dudley's inequality controls E sup Z_θ, or the supremum of increments. A bound on E sup|Z_θ| needs an additional term E|Z_{θ_0}| (or symmetrization).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound E sup|Z_θ| ≤ E|Z_0| + E sup|Z_θ − Z_0|. Since θ=0 gives f_{μ_0}=f_ν, Hoeffding gives E|Z_0| ≤ c(κ,𝒦)/√n. Apply Dudley to the increments, which changes only constants at the same 1/√n rate.
issues.overall_effect: The stated expected generalization bound is not proved as written.
issues.title: Dudley bound applied to sup Z_θ while generalization error is sup |Z_θ|
issues.why_classification: A routine extra O(1/√n) term fixes it; the rate and downstream argument are unchanged.
